xbrli:xbrl.in-capmkt:DisclosureOfNotesOnFinancialRe:
1. The Audited Financial Results for the quarter and six months ended September 30, 2026 have been reviewed by the Audit
Committee and approved by the Board of Directors at their respective meetings held on November 5, 2026.

2. These Audited Financial Results are compi led from the Audited Interim Condensed Financial Statements for the quarter and six months ended September 30, 2026, Audited Interim Condensed Financial Statements for the quarter ended June 30,
2026 and Audited Financial Statements for the year ended March 31 , 2026. The Audited Interim Condensed Financial
Statements for the quarter and six months ended September 30, 2026 have been prepared in accordance with Indian
Accounting Standard ('Ind AS') 34, 'Interim Financial Reporting' as prescribed under Section 133 of the Companies Act,
2013 read together with Rule 3 of the Companies (Indian Accounting Standards) Rules, 2015 (as amended from time to
time) and other accounting principles generally accepted in India.

3. All the amounts included in the Audited Financial Results are rounded off to the nearest million, except per share data and unless stated otherwise. Further, due to rounding off, certain amounts are appearing as '0'.

4. The opening and closing balances in respect of overseas related party transactions (as reflected in this utility) have been converted into INR using the closing conversion rate on March 31, 2026 and September 30, 2026 respectively. Further, the amounts of related party transactions during the half year ended September 30, 2026 have been converted into INR using the average of monthly closing exchange rate of April to September 2026.

5. Airtel Payments Bank Limited (‘APBL’) is a subsidiary company as per the applicable provisions of the Companies Act, 2013. However, under the applicable Indian Accounting Standards (‘Ind AS’), it is classified as an associate company. The relationship with APBL in the above statement is taken as per Ind AS i.e., associate company.

6. To ensure completeness in reporting,the figures have been rounded up to Two decimels.
